note: Schema: game/scripts/sim/FORKS.md. Seed forks written by the sim builder; data agents extend this file.

forks.title: How far should the ground offensive go?
forks.text: Four weeks into the war with Hezbollah, rockets still fall on northern Israel and the army has not cleared the border strip. The security cabinet must decide whether to widen the ground offensive to the Litani River, hold its lines while the UN negotiates, or accept a ceasefire at once. The UN ceasefire of 14 August follows history either way; Lebanese civilians and northern Israeli residents bear the cost of every extra day of fighting.

options.label: Authorise a wider ground offensive up to the Litani River
options.advocate: Defence Minister Amir Peretz

cite.quote: Defence Minister Amir Peretz had proposed the expansion.
Peretz, a proponent of expanding ground operations

lasting.label: Ground forces retrained after the Litani push
Late-war soldier casualties and bereaved northern families

options.note: On 9 August 2006 the security cabinet approved the wider offensive (nine in favour, three abstentions); the UN ceasefire took effect on 14 August.

options.label: Hold current lines, rely on air power and press for a UN ceasefire
options.advocate: Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, reported by Israeli media to fear heavy casualties

cite.quote: Israeli media had said Olmert feared it might entail heavy casualties. Nine ministers approved the move. Three abstained.

lasting.label: Fewer soldiers lost; northern families stay
Hezbollah positions left standing south of the Litani
Hezbollah arsenal keeps the north exposed

options.label: Accept a ceasefire at once and deploy the Lebanese Army in the south
options.advocate: Lebanese Prime Minister Fouad Siniora

cite.quote: Lebanon's prime minister, Fouad Siniora, has since offered to send some 15,000 Lebanese Army troops to the south

lasting.label: Quiet border helps northern business and tourism

forks.title: What shield for the rocket towns?
forks.text: Rockets from Gaza and Lebanon strike Sderot and the north. The Defence Ministry can fund a new short-range interceptor, a laser system offered by a US firm, or no active defence at all. Gaza and Lebanon rocket fire continues either way; the choice decides what protects the towns near the border later.

options.label: Fund Rafael's cheap short-range interceptor (Iron Dome)
options.advocate: Defence Minister Amir Peretz

cite.quote: Largely because it would be an Israeli product, Peretz loved Rafael’s idea.

lasting.label: Defence-engineering cluster spins off civilian technology
Interceptor missiles replenished after each round of fire

options.note: The government approved the project in July 2007 and the Security Cabinet in December 2007; the first combat interception came in April 2011.

options.label: Buy the Northrop Grumman laser system (Nautilus)
options.advocate: Northrop Grumman

cite.quote: One American firm, Northrop Grumman, offered a system that would fire laser beams at incoming rockets.

options.label: Fund no active defence and rely on offensive deterrence
options.advocate: IDF General Staff commanders consulted by the defence minister

cite.quote: When he asked the General Staff commanders in the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) for their opinions, they told him the project was bound to fail
“The Qassam and Katyusha rockets are a problem we’ll have to live with. It’s a tactical issue, not strategic. It won’t destroy the State of Israel.”

lasting.label: Defence budget freed for the wider economy

forks.title: Answering the tent protests
forks.text: After the summer's mass social-justice protests, a committee under Prof. Manuel Trajtenberg has reported on housing, childcare and the cost of living. The cabinet must decide whether to adopt its moderate package, or fund a larger social budget by cutting defence and raising taxes. The protesters' leaders and the defence establishment hold opposing positions on both.

options.label: Adopt the Trajtenberg report, leaving the defence budget largely intact
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu and the Trajtenberg committee

cite.quote: with 21 ministers voting in favor and eight voting against it.

lasting.label: Protest leaders reject the package as too small

options.note: The cabinet approved the report on 9 October 2011 by 21 votes to 8; protest leaders called it inadequate.

options.label: Fund a larger social budget through defence cuts and higher taxes
options.advocate: Protest leader Daphni Leef and National Student Union chair Itzik Shmueli

cite.quote: Leef, who met earlier Sunday with Minister Eli Yishai and thanked him for voting against the report, called on Netanyahu to give the citizens of Israel "a new social budget."
Meanwhile, Chairman of the National Student Union Itzik Shmueli expressed disappointment over the approval of the report

lasting.label: Higher taxes dampen investment and hiring

forks.title: Strike Iran's nuclear sites, or not?
forks.text: Israel's prime minister is lobbying Washington for a credible threat of force against Iran's nuclear programme, while senior former security chiefs argue against a unilateral strike. The cabinet can order preparations for a strike now, or keep to sanctions, covert action and coordination with the United States. Iran's enrichment continues in either case; the choice shapes the risk of regional war.

options.label: Keep to sanctions, covert action and coordination with Washington
options.advocate: Former Mossad chief Meir Dagan

cite.quote: “An attack on Iran before you are exploring all other approaches is not the right way how to do it,” Mr. Dagan told CBS news

lasting.label: Iran's programme advances unchecked by force
Tech sector and research links undisturbed

options.note: Israel did not strike in 2012; it kept pressing for sanctions and for a US military option.

options.label: Order preparations for a unilateral strike on Iran's nuclear sites
options.advocate: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

cite.quote: Netanyahu came to Washington to drum up support for an Iran nuclear strike

lasting.label: Fear of regional war and shelter burden
Researchers and investors leave a country at war

forks.title: Thousands of African asylum seekers
forks.text: Tens of thousands of Eritreans and Sudanese have crossed the Sinai border and settled mostly in south Tel Aviv and Eilat. The cabinet can detain new arrivals under an amended anti-infiltration law, process their asylum claims and let them work, or plan third-country deportation. The arrivals' presence in Israel follows history; their legal status and the strain on host neighbourhoods are the player's call.

options.label: Detain irregular arrivals under the 2012 amendment, later at the Holot centre
options.advocate: Interior Ministry officials and Knesset Interior Committee chair Miri Regev

cite.quote: Israel defines an “infiltrator” as anyone entering Israel irregularly– not through an official border post– including asylum seekers.

lasting.label: Fewer new arrivals in south Tel Aviv
Criticised by UNHCR and rights groups

options.note: A mid-2012 law allowed detention for up to three years; the High Court struck it down in September 2013 and a new law created the Holot centre.

options.label: Process asylum claims individually and grant temporary residence and work permits
options.advocate: Human Rights Watch (Gerry Simpson) and UNHCR

cite.quote: For years, Israel has refused to process Eritrean and Sudanese asylum claims.
Officials should drop this charade of pretending that these extensive restrictions are not detention, and genuinely release the asylum seekers, in line with the High Court ruling.
the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) criticized Israel for pressuring detained Eritreans

lasting.label: Strain on south Tel Aviv neighbourhoods
Arrivals work in hotels and services

options.label: Detain all and deport to a third country
options.advocate: The Interior Minister, as reported in Israeli media in March 2014

cite.quote: the interior minister said he planned to detain all such “infiltrators” and to deport them to a still to be identified third country.

lasting.label: Deportations to a third country criticised
Hotels and services short of labour

forks.title: Speak to Congress about the Iran talks?
forks.text: Speaker John Boehner has invited the prime minister to address Congress on Iran two weeks before Israel's election, without clearing it with the White House. The cabinet can accept, or postpone the speech until after the vote and press the case through quieter channels. The Iran talks continue either way.

options.label: Accept the invitation and address Congress on 3 March
options.advocate: House Speaker John Boehner and Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: “In this time of challenge, I am asking the Prime Minister to address Congress on the grave threats radical Islam and Iran pose to our security and way of life,”

lasting.label: Base rallied by standing up to Washington
Republican allies in Congress back aid

options.note: Netanyahu spoke on 3 March 2015; dozens of Democrats stayed away and the nuclear deal was concluded in July 2015.

options.label: Postpone the address until after the election and lobby quietly
options.advocate: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi and the White House

cite.quote: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi, meanwhile, said it was inappropriate for Boehner to invite Netanyahu to address Congress in the shadow of that election

lasting.label: US research partnerships and grants kept
Less public pressure on the Iran talks
Base feels Israel yielded on Iran

forks.title: The Nation-State Basic Law
forks.text: A Basic Law defining Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people is ready for its final readings. The coalition can pass it as drafted, or add an explicit equality provision first. The law's passage in some form follows the coalition's majority; Arab, Druze and other minority citizens and Jewish supporters hold opposing views on the text.

options.label: Pass the law as drafted
options.advocate: The Netanyahu coalition
options.note: The Knesset passed the law on 19 July 2018 by 62 votes to 55; thousands of Druze protested in Tel Aviv.

options.label: Add an explicit equality clause before passage
options.advocate: Opposition leader Tzipi Livni and Druze community leaders

cite.quote: Opposition leader Tzipi Livni criticised the Netanyahu government for failing to guarantee equality of all Israelis.
The opposition is demanding that the government include a provision guaranteeing equality for all Israeli citizens.

forks.title: Annex parts of the West Bank, or suspend?
forks.text: The coalition agreement allows a vote on applying sovereignty to parts of the West Bank from 1 July under the US peace plan. The cabinet can proceed, delay, or suspend annexation in return for normalisation with the United Arab Emirates. West Bank Palestinians, settlers, Jordan and Gulf states are all affected.

options.label: Suspend annexation in exchange for UAE normalisation
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Trump and the UAE

lasting.label: Gulf normalisation under the Abraham Accords
UAE and Bahrain trade and investment
Settler leaders and right-wing voters disappointed
Settler leaders and right-wing voters feel the pledge was dropped

options.note: On 13 August 2020 Israel agreed to suspend declaring sovereignty; the Abraham Accords with the UAE and Bahrain were signed on 15 September.

options.label: Proceed with applying sovereignty to the Jordan Valley and settlements
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu, who had pledged to annex the Jordan Valley

cite.quote: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to annex part of the occupied West Bank if he is returned to office next week.

lasting.label: Jordan Valley held under Israeli law

options.label: Delay all non-coronavirus business, including annexation
options.advocate: Defence Minister Benny Gantz

cite.quote: Alternate PM says planned 1 July date not ‘sacred’ and Israel should deal with Covid-19 crisis first

lasting.label: Gulf contacts kept open without a deal

forks.title: A coalition with an Arab party?
forks.text: After four inconclusive elections neither bloc has a majority without the Islamist Ra'am party of Mansour Abbas. The party leaders can build the Bennett-Lapid coalition with Ra'am inside it, or try a Netanyahu-led government that Ra'am would back from outside. Arab citizens' budgets and the right-wing parties' red lines are at stake either way.

options.label: Form the Bennett-Lapid coalition with Ra'am inside it
options.advocate: Naftali Bennett, Yair Lapid and Mansour Abbas
options.note: The Bennett-Lapid government, including Ra'am, won a 60-59 Knesset vote on 13 June 2021.

options.label: Form a Netanyahu-led government with Ra'am supporting it from outside
options.advocate: Benjamin Netanyahu and a Ra'am official; Bezalel Smotrich opposed

cite.quote: has decided in principle to back a coalition under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu while remaining outside it

forks.title: The sea border with Lebanon
forks.text: A US-brokered text would set the maritime boundary with Lebanon and let Israel develop the Karish gas field while Lebanon develops Qana. Hezbollah has threatened Karish. The government can sign before the election, or hold the agreement for a Knesset vote first.

options.label: Sign the US-brokered maritime agreement before the election
options.advocate: Prime Minister Yair Lapid

cite.quote: “100% of [Israel’s] security needs, 100% of the Karish reserve, and even some of the profits from the Lebanon reserve”

options.note: The agreement was signed on 27 October 2022.

options.label: Hold the agreement for a Knesset vote before signing
options.advocate: Opposition leader Netanyahu and Interior Minister Ayelet Shaked

cite.quote: Interior Minister Shaked says she would vote against agreement if it is not brought for Knesset approval

forks.title: The judicial overhaul after the protests
forks.text: After weeks of mass protests and a general strike, the coalition's plan to change how judges are chosen and to curb court review faces a decisive Knesset vote. The prime minister can push ahead, pause for talks, or withdraw the bills. Coalition voters who want the reform and protesters who oppose it hold opposing views.

options.label: Pause the legislation and negotiate
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu, with President Herzog hosting talks

cite.quote: Leaders of both Israel’s coalition and opposition have rejected a compromise proposal regarding contentious judicial reform legislation, brokered by Israeli President Isaac Herzog.

lasting.label: Coalition voters see the plan alive

options.note: Netanyahu paused the bills on 27 March 2023; talks at the President's residence ended without agreement.

options.label: Proceed to the final readings
options.advocate: Justice Minister Yariv Levin and coalition hardliners

cite.quote: Justice Minister Yariv Levin, after fighting tooth and nail in recent weeks against a halt to the legislation he led, said it was now up to Netanyahu to decide how to proceed.

options.label: Withdraw the bills
options.advocate: Protest leader Shikma Bressler and Defence Minister Gallant

cite.quote: Shikma Bressler, one of the leaders of the anti-government protest movement, said the campaign would continue until the legislation is canceled.
Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, who had urged the prime minister to put his plan on hold

forks.title: Who gets the gas money?
forks.text: The Tamar and Leviathan finds will make Israel an energy exporter. The state can raise its take through a profits levy, keep the old terms to speed development, or tax and place the revenue in a national fund. Producers and the Sheshinski Committee's supporters hold opposing positions; gas flows from Tamar in 2013 either way.

options.label: Raise the state's take to 52-62% through a profits levy
options.advocate: The Sheshinski Committee, with Bank of Israel Governor Stanley Fischer and Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: The cabinet today approved the Sheshinski committee recommendations to increase the government's take from oil and gas revenue to 52-62%, from the current 33%

lasting.label: Public sees a fair share of the gas

options.note: A tax on oil and gas profits was enacted in 2011 and a sovereign wealth fund law followed in 2014.

options.label: Keep the old royalty terms to speed development
options.advocate: Uri Aldubi, chairman of the Oil and Gas Exploration Industry Association in Israel

cite.quote: Oil and Gas Exploration Industry Association in Israel chairman Uri Aldubi said, "After thousands of years, Israel is again building pyramids in Egypt.

options.label: Raise the take and place gas revenue in a national fund for education and defence
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu, following Governor Fischer's Norwegian-model recommendation

cite.quote: Netanyahu said that he will recommend setting up a national fund for the gas revenues, which will be invested in areas such as education and defense.

lasting.label: Fund invested in education and research

forks.title: COVID-19: how hard to lock down?
forks.text: The virus is spreading. The government can impose nationwide lockdowns, close towns by infection rate (the 'traffic light'), or keep businesses and prayer open with masks and testing. Health officials, Haredi ministers and the economy pull in different directions.

options.label: Nationwide lockdowns
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu and the coronavirus cabinet
options.note: Israel imposed three nationwide lockdowns in 2020-21.

options.label: Targeted closures town by town (the traffic light)
options.advocate: Coronavirus project head Prof. Ronni Gamzu

cite.quote: It is 30 days since the appointment of Prof. Ronni Gamzu as the head of the Ministry of Health's campaign to eliminate the virus and he is not making very much headway. He is being attacked on all sides by politicians. Last Thursday he presented the Covid-19 cabinet with his "traffic light" proposal in which every local authority would be given a color according to its infection rate with restrictions imposed on red locations.

lasting.label: Fewer lost workdays than a full lockdown

options.label: Keep businesses and prayer open with masks and testing
options.advocate: Housing Minister Yaakov Litzman and Haredi MKs

cite.quote: Minister of Construction and Housing Yaakov Litzman called on Gamzu to resign for claiming that this could cause a further spread of the disease.

But his ideas were fiercely attacked by haredi ultra-orthodox MKs and the meeting broke up without any agreements. Gamzu's opponents insist that his plan would involve discrimination against haredi communities.

forks.title: Olmert's offer to Abbas, or an economic track?
forks.text: After the Annapolis conference, Prime Minister Olmert is in talks with Abbas on borders, Jerusalem and refugees while facing corruption investigations and an election. He can table a comprehensive offer now, or shelve the final-status issues and concentrate on the Palestinian economy and security. Abbas not signing and Olmert leaving office follow history either way; the player decides what Israel puts on the table.

options.label: Table a comprehensive offer on borders, Jerusalem and refugees
options.advocate: Prime Minister Ehud Olmert

cite.quote: On the 16th of September, 2008, I presented him (Abbas) with a comprehensive plan.

lasting.label: Israel seen offering a two-state deal
Right-wing voters reject concessions on Jerusalem
Investors price in a settlement track

options.note: Olmert presented a map and plan to Abbas on 16 September 2008; Abbas did not sign, the talks lapsed, and Olmert left office in March 2009.

options.label: Shelve final-status issues and focus on the West Bank economy and security
options.advocate: Likud leader Benjamin Netanyahu

cite.quote: Netanyahu spokeswoman Dina Libster said, adding that the Likud leader believes that talks with the Palestinians should focus on economic issues.

lasting.label: West Bank trade and joint economic projects
Voters reassured that Jerusalem is not on the table

forks.title: A coalition built on equal burden
forks.text: After the January election Yair Lapid (Yesh Atid) and Naftali Bennett (Jewish Home) have pledged to enter government only together, with Lapid demanding equal sharing of military service. Netanyahu can accept their terms and form a coalition without the Haredi parties, or build one around Shas and United Torah Judaism and keep the draft exemption. Netanyahu stays prime minister either way.

options.label: Form a coalition with Yesh Atid and Jewish Home, without the Haredi parties
options.advocate: Yair Lapid and Naftali Bennett

cite.quote: the conditions set by Yair Lapid for joining the coalition - equal sharing of the military service burden
Netanyahu will probably be compelled to forgo the haredi (ultra-orthodox) parties in the next government coalition.

lasting.label: Draft and work incentives push more Haredi men to jobs
Haredi parties in opposition and street protests
Child allowances cut for large families

options.note: The Likud Beiteinu-Yesh Atid-Jewish Home coalition was sworn in on 18 March 2013 with the Haredi parties in opposition.

options.label: Build a coalition around Shas and United Torah Judaism and keep the exemption
options.advocate: Shas leader Eli Yishai

cite.quote: an entire sector, traditional and religious, was boycotted solely for its beliefs and perceptions

lasting.label: Child allowances and Haredi community framework kept
Exemption keeps the army short of recruits

forks.title: Prisoner releases to restart the talks
forks.text: Secretary of State Kerry has brought both sides to the table, and the Palestinians want pre-1993 prisoners freed in stages as the price of talks. The cabinet can approve the release of 104 prisoners in four batches tied to progress, or refuse any release and let the talks collapse. Settlement and borders issues remain open either way.

options.label: Approve the staged release of 104 prisoners tied to the talks
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: The decision to release prisoners is one of the toughest decisions that I've made as prime minister,

lasting.label: European research and trade ties kept
Bereaved families and the right protest

options.note: The cabinet approved the release on 28 July 2013 by 13 votes to 7; three batches were freed and the fourth was withheld in April 2014 as the talks collapsed.

options.label: Refuse any prisoner release
options.advocate: Economy Minister Naftali Bennett

cite.quote: The goal is to establish a red line once and for all

lasting.label: EU research funding and cooperation put at risk

forks.title: Zero VAT for first-time buyers
forks.text: Housing prices have risen sharply since 2008. Finance Minister Lapid proposes removing the 18% VAT on a first new apartment for buyers who have served, while the Bank of Israel warns it will lift demand. The cabinet can adopt the plan, or drop it and put land and tenders for lower prices first.

options.label: Adopt zero VAT on a first apartment for eligible buyers
options.advocate: Finance Minister Yair Lapid

cite.quote: The state of Israel decided today that it's going to stop profiting off the children of the middle class.

lasting.label: Young families buy homes and have children

options.note: The plan passed the ministerial committee on 23 March 2014 but was not carried out in full; the Knesset dissolved in December 2014.

options.label: Reject the VAT cut and expand land and price-linked tenders
options.advocate: Bank of Israel Governor Karnit Flug and Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: the sudden lowering of housing costs would create a spike in demand
All contractors will get [state] land at lower prices if they guarantee lower final-sale prices,

lasting.label: More land released and more building
Young buyers get no immediate relief
Fewer young families can afford homes

forks.title: The Azaria verdict: pardon or not?
forks.text: Sergeant Elor Azaria has been convicted of manslaughter for shooting a wounded Palestinian attacker in Hebron, and many Israelis support him. The army and the president can let the sentence stand and consider leniency later, or grant an immediate pardon. The conviction itself follows the court's ruling.

options.label: Let the military court's sentence stand and refuse a pardon
options.advocate: IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot

cite.quote: didn't accept responsibility

lasting.label: Rule of law and army ethics upheld
Command discipline and rules of engagement kept
Supporters of the soldier feel abandoned

options.note: Azaria was sentenced to 18 months; Eisenkot cut it by four months and refused a pardon. He was freed in May 2018 after nine months.

options.label: Grant an immediate pardon
options.advocate: Education Minister Naftali Bennett

cite.quote: The security of the citizens of Israel requires an immediate pardon for Elor Azaria, who was sent to protect us.

lasting.label: Seen abroad as shielding unlawful killing
Command authority over rules of engagement weakened

forks.title: Metal detectors on the Temple Mount
forks.text: After two police officers were killed at the Temple Mount on 14 July, the government installed metal detectors at the entrances. Muslim worshippers are boycotting the site and Jordan and the Palestinian Authority are protesting. The security cabinet can keep the detectors or replace them with camera-based checks.

options.label: Remove the detectors and use camera-based 'smart checks'
options.advocate: The security bodies and Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: accepted the recommendation of all of the security bodies
I must make decisions coolly and judiciously.

lasting.label: Tension with Jordan and the PA eased

options.note: On 25 July 2017 the security cabinet removed the detectors and approved up to NIS 100 million for smart checks.

options.label: Keep the detectors in place
options.advocate: Public Security Minister Gilad Erdan

cite.quote: Public Security Minister Gilad Erdan told Channel 2 that "once the red line has been crossed of automatic weapons on the Temple Mount [as in last Friday's terrorist attack], there is a need to change the security arrangements."

lasting.label: Weapons screened at the Temple Mount
Prayer boycott and protests in East Jerusalem

forks.title: After the Winograd report
forks.text: The Winograd Commission's final report finds 'grave failings' in the decisions of the 2006 Lebanon war, at the military and political levels. Bereaved families and reservists call for the prime minister to go, and the Labor leader and Defence Minister had earlier said he would force an early election if the report was damning. The report's findings are fixed; whether the government and its leaders carry on is the cabinet's call.

options.label: Keep the coalition and the prime minister in office and press on with rebuilding the army
options.advocate: Defence Minister Ehud Barak and Prime Minister Ehud Olmert

cite.quote: But on Sunday Barak said he had decided to stay on as defense minister because of the serious security challenges Israel faces from Gaza, Hezbollah, Syria and Iran

lasting.label: Defence Minister stays to rehabilitate the army
Bereaved families and reservists see no accountability
Public trust in leaders' accountability after the war

options.note: Barak announced on 3 February 2008 that Labor would stay in the coalition; Olmert remained prime minister until he resigned over corruption allegations later in 2008.

options.label: The prime minister takes responsibility and resigns
options.advocate: Bereaved families of the 2006 war

cite.quote: Many bereaved families have joined together in their grief and are spearheading a movement to try to get Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to take personal responsibility for the war's failures and resign.

lasting.label: Leaders seen to take responsibility for a failed war
Leadership change delays budget and reforms
Defence reform stalls during the transition

options.label: Labor leaves the coalition and forces early elections
options.advocate: Defence Minister Ehud Barak, who had earlier pledged to do so

cite.quote: Mr. Barak has said in the past that if Olmert came out looking reprehensible in the final Winograd Report, he would force Israel to hold early elections to drive Olmert from office.

lasting.label: Voters, not the cabinet, settle accountability
Annapolis talks paused for a campaign
Caretaker government in a rocket-fire year
Fresh mandate for budgets and reform

forks.title: Answering the Goldstone report
forks.text: A UN fact-finding mission led by Richard Goldstone accuses both Israel and Hamas of possible war crimes in the 2008-09 Gaza operation (Cast Lead). Goldstone himself says an independent Israeli inquiry 'would be the end of the matter', while the army opposes one. The report's existence is fixed; how Israel answers it is the cabinet's call.

options.label: Rely on the army's own probes and a ministerial task force; no commission of inquiry
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu, Defence Minister Barak and the IDF

cite.quote: "No soldiers or officers will be brought before a commission of inquiry," Netanyahu said.
But Defense Minister Ehud Barak and the Israel Defense Forces are strongly against such an inquiry.

lasting.label: Chain of command spared civilian inquiry
UN follow-up and possible ICC referral stay open
Allegations left to the army's own probes

options.note: Netanyahu set up a ministerial task force under Justice Minister Neeman and ruled out a commission of inquiry; the IDF kept investigating complaints itself.

options.label: Appoint an independent civilian commission of inquiry into the Gaza operation
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Avigdor Lieberman, Deputy Prime Minister Dan Meridor and Rabbis for Human Rights

cite.quote: several members of the Israeli government, including Foreign Minister Avigdor Lieberman, are advising Netanyahu to go that route.
Earlier this week, Israeli Deputy Prime Minister Dan Meridor said Israel should launch a "commission of inquiry or examination" to investigate war crimes charges.

lasting.label: Credible inquiry closes the UN process
Officers weigh legal exposure in planning and training

options.label: Keep the army's probes but add a committee of jurists and former generals to scrutinise them
options.advocate: Attorney General Menachem Mazuz

cite.quote: Mazuz has proposed relying on its internal probes into the allegations of war crimes, but adding credibility by establishing a committee of jurists and ex-generals to scrutinize the IDF’s work

lasting.label: Army probes stay in army hands

forks.title: Who investigates the flotilla raid?
forks.text: Nine activists died when naval commandos boarded the Mavi Marmara bound for Gaza. UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon proposes an international commission under former New Zealand prime minister Geoffrey Palmer, while the prime minister prefers an Israeli inquiry. The raid and its deaths are fixed; the format of the investigation is the cabinet's call.

options.label: Appoint an Israeli public commission under Justice Turkel with two foreign observers
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: Israel’s Cabinet unanimously approved a commission of inquiry into the interception of a Gaza-bound flotilla that left nine passengers dead.

lasting.label: Blockade and boarding doctrine reviewed in-house
Cabinet united behind a national probe
Turkish trade and tourism ties damaged

options.note: The cabinet approved the Turkel Commission on 14 June 2010; it later found the blockade and the raid lawful under international law, and Israel took part in a separate UN panel under Palmer.

options.label: Accept the UN secretary-general's international commission under Geoffrey Palmer
options.advocate: UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon

cite.quote: U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon on Saturday night proposed a commission of inquiry headed by former New Zealand Prime Minister Geoffrey Palmer

lasting.label: Turkish trade and relations repaired sooner
Boarding doctrine open to international findings
Public sees outsiders judging the army

forks.title: The gas outline for Leviathan
forks.text: Noble Energy froze Leviathan after the Antitrust Commissioner warned he might break up its partnership with Delek. The prime minister proposes an outline letting the partners keep the field if they sell Tamar and smaller holdings; critics want a break-up or state ownership. Gas supply to Israel, Egypt and Jordan depends on the field, and the price Israelis pay depends on who owns it.

options.label: Approve the outline: the partners keep Leviathan but sell their other fields
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: Netanyahu has proposed the Gas Outline, which would permit Noble-Delek to retain majority control of Leviathan for 10 years after the gas begins flowing in exchange for reducing its holdings in Tamar and two of the smaller fields.

lasting.label: Leviathan developed; gas exports to Egypt and Jordan
Tax and royalty income from Leviathan
Public sees a private monopoly protected

options.note: The government and Knesset approved the outline in 2015; the High Court later upheld it, with a clause removed, and Leviathan began production in December 2019.

options.label: Back the Antitrust Commissioner and break up the Noble-Delek partnership
options.advocate: Antitrust Commissioner David Gilo

cite.quote: a year ago, Antitrust Commissioner David Gilo warned that he was considering breaking up the partnership.

lasting.label: Leviathan frozen while ownership is resolved
Competing owners bring gas to market later

options.label: Nationalise the gas fields
options.advocate: The gas protest movement, led by organiser Orly Bar Lev

cite.quote: protesters have gathered weekly, sometimes by the thousands, to urge Israel to nationalize the fields.
said Orly Bar Lev, a protest organizer.

lasting.label: Gas seen as a public asset

forks.title: Reconciliation with Turkey
forks.text: After six years without ambassadors, Israel and Turkey have a reconciliation text: an Israeli compensation fund for the Mavi Marmara families, a Turkish law closing claims, and Turkish building projects in Gaza via Ashdod port. The Security Cabinet must vote. The raid itself is fixed; whether ties are restored is the cabinet's call.

options.label: Approve the reconciliation agreement and restore ties
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: “Israel has made an important strategic agreement in terms of security, regional stability and the Israeli economy,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday afternoon in Rome

lasting.label: Turkish trade and gas-pipeline talks reopen

options.note: The Security Cabinet approved the deal 7-3 on 29 June 2016; ambassadors returned in 2016 and were withdrawn again in 2018.

options.label: Reject the agreement
options.advocate: Defence Minister Avigdor Liberman, Education Minister Naftali Bennett and Justice Minister Ayelet Shaked

forks.title: Amona and the Regulation Bill
forks.text: The High Court has ordered the Amona outpost, built on private Palestinian land, evacuated by 25 December. Jewish Home pushes a Regulation Bill to legalise such outposts with compensation for owners, over the prime minister's objections and the attorney general's warning that he cannot defend it. The court order is fixed; how the government responds is the cabinet's call.

options.note: Amona was evacuated on 1-2 February 2017 after a final court extension; the state approved thousands of new settlement homes.

forks.title: A coalition that cannot be built
forks.text: The right-wing parties won 65 seats in April, yet Yisrael Beiteinu will join only if the haredi draft bill passes as written, and the haredi parties will join only if it is softened. The prime minister's deadline to form a government expires at midnight. The April result is fixed; how the deadlock ends is the Knesset's call.

forks.title: Rules of fire on the Gaza fence
forks.text: Organisers in Gaza have called weekly mass marches to the border fence from 30 March. The army plans snipers and live fire against attempts to breach it, and the left-wing opposition wants the rules of engagement examined. The marches and the army's presence follow history either way; the cabinet decides whether the rules are reviewed.

options.note: The army kept its rules and the marches continued weekly until December 2019; the defence minister said there would be no international inquiry.

forks.text: The September 2019 election left neither Likud nor Blue and White able to form a majority. forks.title: The Bennett-Lapid coalition loses its majority
forks.text: After defections and a failed vote to extend West Bank legal regulations, the coalition has lost its majority. The prime minister and foreign minister can fast-track a Knesset dissolution bill, or the House Committee chair can delay it so the opposition may try to form an alternative government. Netanyahu leads the opposition and the election date depends on the choice.
